data.narrative:
Quantum Machines is a Series C quantum computing company that has raised $280M to date. The quantum computing peer universe consists of 11 companies total—3 public (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum, IonQ's private predecessor stage, and Infleqtion—though few peers operate at identical stage and valuation tiers.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach here. Using total raised ($280M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.7x multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $476M. Peer-median analysis cannot be reliably applied; while five quantum computing companies exist in the broader dataset, none satisfy the narrower filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) needed to establish a meaningful comparable set of three or more firms. Using all-sector medians would introduce distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $405M to $547M, with $476M as the midpoint estimate. This range reflects ±15% sensitivity around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the relative maturity of Quantum Machines' technology versus the broader peer set, near-term capital efficiency, and the absence of direct same-stage quantum computing comparables to validate the step-up multiplier. The single-method foundation should be supplemented with additional data as more peers mature into adjacent funding rounds.
